From f2a880e802ad12d1e38039d1334fb1475d0f5241 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Date: Thu, 29 Jan 2026 23:29:37 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] tty: hvc_iucv: fix off-by-one in number of supported devices

MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES == HVC_ALLOC_TTY_ADAPTERS == 8.
This is the number of entries in:
  static struct hvc_iucv_private *hvc_iucv_table[MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES];

Sometimes hvc_iucv_table[] is limited by:
(a)	if (num > hvc_iucv_devices) // for error detection
or
(b)	for (i = 0; i < hvc_iucv_devices; i++) // in 2 places
(so these 2 don't agree; second one appears to be correct to me.)

hvc_iucv_devices can be 0..8. This is a counter.
(c)	if (hvc_iucv_devices > MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES)

If hvc_iucv_devices == 8, (a) allows the code to access hvc_iucv_table[8].
Oops.

Fixes: 44a01d5ba8a4 ("[S390] s390/hvc_console: z/VM IUCV hypervisor console support")
Signed-off-by: Randy Dunlap <rdunlap@infradead.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260130072939.1535869-1-rdunlap@infradead.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c b/drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c
index 1dcdb9e99bd8..37db8a3e5158 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c
@@ -130,7 +130,7 @@ static struct iucv_handler hvc_iucv_handler = {
  */
 static struct hvc_iucv_private *hvc_iucv_get_private(uint32_t num)
 {
-	if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)
+	if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)
 		return NULL;
 	return hvc_iucv_table[num];
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes an off-by-one error in the file `drivers/tty/hvc/hvc_iucv.c`. The only modification is within the `hvc_iucv_get_private()` function: the boundary condition `num > hvc_iucv_devices` is changed to `num >= hvc_iucv_devices`. This change ensures that when `hvc_iucv_devices` equals the maximum number of devices (`MAX_HVC_IUCV_LINES`, which is 8), the index `num` cannot access `hvc_iucv_table[8]` (which is out of bounds because the array has indices 0–7). Previously, the old condition allowed accessing the element at index 8 when `hvc_iucv_devices` was 8, causing an out-of-bounds read. The fix tightens the check to prevent any access beyond the allocated array.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
if (num > hvc_iucv_devices)
```
Reason: 
`hvc_iucv_devices` is the count of valid entries (0 to 8). Valid array indices for `hvc_iucv_table[]` are 0 to `hvc_iucv_devices - 1`. Using `>` allows accessing index equal to `hvc_iucv_devices` (e.g., 8), which is one past the last valid element, causing an out‑of‑bounds access.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
if (num >= hvc_iucv_devices)
```
Reason: 
Changing `>` to `>=` correctly rejects any index that is equal to or greater than the count, so only indices strictly less than `hvc_iucv_devices` are allowed. This prevents the off‑by‑one error and aligns with the correct loop condition `i < hvc_iucv_devices` used elsewhere.
